The L-1A new office petition is the most powerful route for business owners and multinational executives to expand to the United States. USCIS requires proof of a physical US office, a credible USCIS-compliant business plan, a documented qualifying corporate relationship, and a realistic staffing plan within the first year. Most advisory firms stop at the petition. USAIS goes further — we physically set up your US branch or subsidiary, secure your office space, open your business bank account, and file an I-129 petition built to get approved.

Step by Step
Our L-1A New Office Process — 3 Steps to Your US Business

From company setup to USCIS approval — we manage every step of your L-1A new office petition so you can focus on building your business.

01
Step 1
📋
Business Assessment & Initial Eligibility Check

Before anything else, we assess whether your business qualifies for an L-1A new office petition. We review your corporate structure, confirm the qualifying relationship between your foreign company and the proposed US entity, and verify your role meets USCIS's executive or managerial standard.

⚡ Quick Eligibility Check — Do You Qualify for the L-1A Visa?
Check Now

Your business is likely a strong L-1A candidate if it meets the following criteria:

  • ✓Operating for at least 2 years — your foreign company must have been actively trading for a minimum of 2 years
  • ✓3 or more employees on payroll — USCIS expects a genuine business with an active workforce, not a one-person operation
  • ✓Profitable and financially stable — the business must be in a profitable stage with a healthy financial track record
  • ✓Annual turnover of approx. ₹1 Crore or more (preferred) — demonstrates the financial strength to support a new US operation
⚠ These are preferred qualifying indicators, not absolute USCIS thresholds. Every case is unique — schedule a free consultation for a personalised eligibility assessment.
💼
This is a Business Visa — Not an Investment Visa.

You do not need huge financials or a large capital investment. What USCIS looks for is a genuine, operating business with real employees, real revenue, and a credible plan to expand to the US. If your business is running and generating income, you likely qualify.

Corporate structure & relationship review

Step 2

Company Setup in the US

We form your US branch, subsidiary, or affiliate entity — LLC or C-Corp — and handle everything needed to make it USCIS-ready: EIN registration, US business banking, Registered Agent, state compliance filings, and most importantly, securing a signed physical office lease at our Fremont, California headquarters or a suitable commercial location. Your US company is fully operational before we file your petition.

EIN, bank account & Registered Agent

03
Step 3
📊
USCIS-Compliant Business Plan

Our in-house business plan writers produce a USCIS-compliant L-1A new office business plan that satisfies exactly what USCIS adjudicators look for. This is not a generic business plan — it is built specifically to win your L-1A petition. We include realistic financial projections, a US market opportunity analysis, a first-year staffing plan, evidence of sufficient funding, and a clear description of your executive or managerial role.

Step 4

Petition Filing to USCIS

We compile and file your complete L-1A new office petition with USCIS — Form I-129, the full evidentiary package, and your USCIS-compliant business plan. We also handle any RFE (Request for Evidence) responses if issued, and manage all USCIS correspondence from start to approval.

Common Questions
Frequently Asked Questions
An L-1A new office petition allows a foreign company to send a qualifying manager or executive to the US to set up a new subsidiary, affiliate, or branch. USCIS requires proof of a physical office space and a credible, compliant business plan.
Yes. USCIS requires a signed lease or deed for a physical US office before approving the petition. USAIS helps you secure appropriate space in any of our 16 US office cities.
Standard processing takes 2–4 months. With Premium Processing (Form I-907), USCIS is required to make a decision within 15 business days. USAIS recommends premium processing for all new office petitions.
Yes. After 1 year of successful US operations, the L-1A holder can apply for an EB-1C Multinational Manager/Executive green card — no PERM labor certification required. USAIS plans your EB-1C pathway from day one.
A compliant USCIS business plan includes an executive summary, market analysis, 5-year financial projections, US staffing plan, management structure, and supporting company financials. USAIS prepares all of this entirely in-house.
